text: Scoreboard. Look at the scoreboard. You're in second place!
Timer. The timer said twenty seconds, and I took off.
Spectator. The spectators on the beach were screaming.
Tie. It was almost a tie with the surfer in white.
Shaky. My legs were shaky the whole time.
Relief. When I saw my score, what a relief!
Interview. The commentator wants a quick interview at the tent.
Hug. Kai gave me a big hug on the sand.
Nobody caught anything for ten minutes.
Everybody on the beach was watching.
I didn't hear anything out there.
Mate, that was crazy! Nobody caught anything for ten minutes.
I know. It was so flat. My legs were shaky the whole time.
But you didn't panic. Everybody on the beach was watching you.
Really? I didn't hear anything out there. Did anybody film my last wave?
I did. Look. The timer said twenty seconds, and you took off.
Is there anything new on the scoreboard? It still shows the old scores.
Not yet. But the spectators went wild. Somebody next to me screamed your name!
What if it's a tie with the guy in white?
Then the judges look at the best wave. And your last wave was the best thing in the heat.
Okay. I can't look. Tell me when something changes.
Did anybody film my last wave?
We're in the final. What a relief!

Good morning again, everybody, and thanks for waiting. Something was wrong with the scoreboard, but everything is fine now. Here are the results of heat two. It was a strange heat. For the first ten minutes, nobody caught anything. The ocean was completely flat. Then the sets came. In first place, with fourteen points, Jack Moore from Margaret River. And in second place, with a wave in the last twenty seconds, Renato Lara from Perth, with twelve point five. Is anybody here from the Perth squad? Yes, I can hear you! Both surfers go through to tomorrow's final. Renato, please come to the tent for a quick interview.

Renato, it's Dana. I'm sorry I wasn't at the tent with you. Somebody from the club needed help with the van. What a relief! When the scoreboard changed, I hugged everybody near me, even people I don't know! Listen. You didn't do anything wrong today. You waited, and you didn't waste anything. Tonight there's nothing to prepare. Just eat something good and rest. The final is tomorrow at ten. There are only four surfers in it, and everybody is good. But you deserve to be there. See you at the campsite.
